subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should this allow-always data-loss issue be fixed by finishing the broader CAS/locking exec-approval repair, or by landing a narrower concurrent allow-always persistence fix first?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the repair changes persisted exec approval security state and overlaps an open blocked PR for a related stale-writeback security issue.

options.title: Finish shared CAS/locking repair
options.body: Use the broader exec approval write-consistency path to cover allow-always persistence and usage metadata together, then close this issue and the related stale-writeback issue when proof passes.

options.title: Split a narrow allow-always fix
options.body: Land a small focused repair for concurrent allow-always additions now, while leaving stale usage metadata and revoked-policy restore work to the related security issue.

options.title: Defer to storage migration
options.body: Wait for a larger database-backed exec approvals migration, accepting that users can keep losing allowlist entries until that work lands.

recommendation.title: Finish shared CAS/locking repair
recommendation.body: Use the broader exec approval write-consistency path to cover allow-always persistence and usage metadata together, then close this issue and the related stale-writeback issue when proof passes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest connection to exec approvals, gateway approval decisions, and node policy merging.
